bg_facts: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow on Nov 10.

slides.title: What *happened*
slides.body: On November 10, Anthropic, the company behind Claude, started the roadshow for its stock market debut. It plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

slides.title: The *numbers*
slides.body: At the top of the range the sale brings in up to about $64.4 billion. Anthropic sells 801.4 million new shares. Existing holders sell 23.6 million, and Anthropic gets none of that money. A separate $26 billion private investment closes after the IPO.

slides.title: What it is *worth*
slides.body: About $1 trillion based on shares outstanding, and up to $1.4 trillion when stock options and similar shares are counted. SpaceX's IPO in June raised $86 billion, the record this one comes close to.

slides.title: The *business*
slides.body: Revenue in the first 9 months of 2026 was $33.2 billion, per the filing. Anthropic has also signed up for nearly $900 billion in computing deals and leases with partners like Amazon and Google, spread over many years.

slides.title: What is *not set*
slides.body: The final price can still move inside or outside the range. Anthropic has not confirmed a first trading day. Its filing is not yet effective, so no shares can be bought or sold yet. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the deal.

slides.title: What it means *for you*
slides.body: Your Claude app and plan work the same today. If you are thinking about buying the stock, new listings can swing hard in the first weeks, so read the prospectus first. News, not financial advice.
